title: Open gluing for Noetherian adic formal schemes and ideals
statement: A Noetherian adic formal scheme means a locally topologically ringed space with a finite cover by $\operatorname{Spf}R$, for Noetherian rings $R$ complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal; its structure sheaf is the inverse limit of the sheaves on the quotient spectra [def-per-adic-formal-geometry]. Morphisms are continuous local morphisms of these topologically ringed spaces. A coherent ideal is locally the completed-localization sheaf of a finitely generated ring ideal. Let $(\mathfrak T_i)_{i\in E}$ be a finite family of such formal schemes, including the empty family. For each $i,j$, let $\mathfrak T_{ij}\subseteq\mathfrak T_i$ be open and let $\phi_{ij}:\mathfrak T_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak T_{ji}$ be an isomorphism. Assume $\mathfrak T_{ii}=\mathfrak T_i$, $\phi_{ii}=1$, $\phi_{ji}=\phi_{ij}^{-1}$, and that $\phi_{ij}$ identifies $\mathfrak T_{ij}\cap\mathfrak T_{ik}$ with $\mathfrak T_{ji}\cap\mathfrak T_{jk}$, with $\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}=\phi_{ik}$ on this triple overlap. There is a Noetherian adic formal scheme $\mathfrak T$, unique up to unique isomorphism respecting the gluing maps, with open immersions $u_i:\mathfrak T_i\to\mathfrak T$ covering $\mathfrak T$ and identifying precisely the indicated overlaps. Compatible morphisms from these pieces to any adic formal scheme glue uniquely, and equality of morphisms is local on a formal open cover of the source. Compatible coherent ideals glue uniquely as ideal subsheaves; compatible ideals of definition glue to an ideal of definition, and compatible open coherent ideals glue to an open coherent ideal. The resulting objects, morphisms and ideals commute with restriction to open subsets and refinement of covers. Overlaps need not be affine.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, definition as locally topologically ringed spaces and affine-open gluing; Tag 01JA, section-glueing-schemes, topological and sheaf gluing construction (applied to the complete topological ring sheaves of the formal charts). Coherence and openness are the local predicates explicitly specified here.

proof.text: Form $T=(\coprod_i|\mathfrak T_i|)/\sim$, where $(i,x)\sim(j,y)$ means $x\in\mathfrak T_{ij}$ and $y=\phi_{ij}(x)$. Reflexivity is the diagonal identity, symmetry is the inverse identity, and transitivity follows because $\phi_{ij}(x)\in\mathfrak T_{ji}\cap\mathfrak T_{jk}$ forces $x\in\mathfrak T_{ij}\cap\mathfrak T_{ik}$ and then $\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}(x)=\phi_{ik}(x)$. Give $T$ the topology in which $W$ is open precisely when all $u_i^{-1}W$ are open. Write $U_i=u_i(|\mathfrak T_i|)$. Each $u_i$ is injective, $u_j^{-1}U_i=\mathfrak T_{ji}$, and $u_j^{-1}u_i(V)=\phi_{ji}^{-1}(V\cap\mathfrak T_{ij})$ for open $V\subseteq|\mathfrak T_i|$. Thus $u_i$ identifies its source homeomorphically with the open $U_i$, and $U_i\cap U_j=u_i(\mathfrak T_{ij})$. This uses no affine property of the overlaps.

source.place: Tag 01JB, lemma-glue, quotient-space construction; Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, topological sheaves and locally topologically ringed spaces

proof.text: Transport $\mathcal O_{\mathfrak T_i}$ along $u_i$ to $U_i$. The structure maps of $\phi_{ij}$, inverted if necessary to orient descent from $i$ to $j$, give isomorphisms of sheaves of topological rings on $U_i\cap U_j$; the given cocycle gives their cocycle. Apply [lem-per-topological-ring-sheaf-open-descent] to obtain $\mathcal O_T$, with its matching-tuples section topology and compatible topological ring sheaf isomorphisms on the $U_i$. For $x=u_i(y)$ the open-neighbourhood germ identification gives $\mathcal O_{T,x}\cong\mathcal O_{\mathfrak T_i,y}$, so the stalk is local. Hence $(T,\mathcal O_T)$ is locally topologically ringed, the $u_i$ are open immersions, and their overlap maps are exactly $\phi_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 01JB, lemma-glue, quotient-space construction; Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, topological sheaves and locally topologically ringed spaces

proof.text: Choose the finite formal affine cover of each $\mathfrak T_i$ in the definition [def-per-adic-formal-geometry]. Its images under the open isomorphisms $u_i$ are the same formal affine topological ringed spaces in $T$. The union of these finitely many finite covers is finite and covers $T$, so $\mathfrak T=(T,\mathcal O_T)$ is a Noetherian adic formal scheme. All complete coordinate rings, ideals of definition and quotient-limit presentations are unchanged on these charts. If the family is empty, $T=\varnothing$ and the unique sheaf of topological rings has the one-element ring on its only open. It has the empty formal affine cover and satisfies the conclusion; empty individual pieces cause no change.

source.place: Tag 01JB, lemma-glue, quotient-space construction; Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, topological sheaves and locally topologically ringed spaces

proof.text: For compatible morphisms $f_i:\mathfrak T_i\to\mathfrak Y$, define $f(u_i(x))=f_i(x)$. Compatibility makes this well defined; the topology of Step 1 makes it continuous. On an open $V\subseteq\mathfrak Y$, send $s\in\mathcal O_{\mathfrak Y}(V)$ to the tuple $(f_i^\sharp(s))_i$ on $f_i^{-1}V$. This tuple is compatible and gives $f^\sharp_V(s)\in\mathcal O_T(f^{-1}V)$ by the section formula in [lem-per-topological-ring-sheaf-open-descent]. Each coordinate is continuous, so this map into the product, and then its subspace of compatible tuples, is continuous. Ring operations and restriction commute coordinatewise. The stalk map at $u_i(x)$ is the local stalk map of $f_i$, hence $f$ is a formal morphism. A second extension has the same point map and the same section coordinates, so equals $f$. The same argument on any open cover of a source proves locality of equality. Applying this to the two sets of gluing maps for two candidate gluings gives inverse morphisms, since their composites restrict to identities. This proves uniqueness up to unique isomorphism respecting all charts.

source.place: Tag 01JB, lemma-glue, quotient-space construction; Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, topological sheaves and locally topologically ringed spaces

proof.text: Identify each local ideal with an ideal subsheaf $\mathcal J_i\subseteq\mathcal O_T|_{U_i}$. Define $\mathcal J(W)=\{s\in\mathcal O_T(W):s|_{W\cap U_i}\in\mathcal J_i(W\cap U_i)\text{ for all }i\}$. Restrictions preserve this condition. If sections in $\mathcal J$ agree on an open cover of $W$, their unique glue in $\mathcal O_T(W)$ belongs to $\mathcal J$: on every $W\cap U_i$ this follows from the sheaf axiom of $\mathcal J_i$. Addition and multiplication by ring sections preserve the condition, so $\mathcal J$ is an ideal subsheaf. On $W\subseteq U_i$ compatibility of the ideals says exactly that the condition for $i$ implies all the others; hence $\mathcal J|_{U_i}=\mathcal J_i$. Conversely, membership in any ideal subsheaf with these restrictions is this same condition, by its sheaf axiom. This proves equality uniqueness as subsheaves, rather than just abstract isomorphism uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 00AL, sheaves.tex lemma-glue-sheaves, matching sections specialized to subobjects

proof.text: The given coherence convention is local: near each point in some $U_i$, the restriction of $\mathcal J$ is exactly the completed-localization sheaf of the given finitely generated ring ideal representing $\mathcal J_i$. Thus the glued ideal is coherent. Here an open ideal is locally an ideal containing a power of the chart ideal of definition, and an ideal of definition is locally an open ideal whose powers generate the given adic topology. These are the usual local predicates on a formal scheme, not a demand that sections on every non-quasi-compact open have one uniform adic exponent. For the glued ideal the same charts and powers that verify either predicate for $\mathcal J_i$ verify it for $\mathcal J$. Therefore compatible ideals of definition give an ideal of definition, and compatible open coherent ideals give an open coherent ideal. No ideal-algebraization, formal-functions theorem or extension from the overlap to a whole affine chart is used.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, ideals of definition and section topologies; local coherence convention of the item

proof.text: For an open $W\subseteq T$, use the restricted pieces $u_i^{-1}W$, the restricted transition maps, and $\mathcal O_T|_W$. The underlying quotient, section tuples, morphism coordinates and ideal membership formula of Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 are exactly their restrictions to $W$. The restrictions are again Noetherian formal schemes: in any original $\operatorname{Spf}(R,K)$, cover its part of $W$ by principal opens $D(s)\cap V(K)$. By [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement] each is $\operatorname{Spf}R_{\{s\}}$ with Noetherian coordinate ring $R_{\{s\}}$, the $KR_s$-adic completion of $R_s$. Since $KR_s$ is finitely generated, [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] (with $A=M=R_s$, $I=KR_s$) shows $R_{\{s\}}$ is complete and separated for the finitely generated ideal $KR_{\{s\}}$, so each is a formal affine open. Only finitely many are needed: the ideal generated by all these $s$ is finitely generated, and writing finitely many generators as finite sums selects finitely many original $s$ with the same generated ideal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; their union of principal opens is therefore the same. There are only finitely many original charts. Thus restriction remains inside the finite-cover convention, even though the overlaps were not assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 01JB, lemma-glue, quotient-space construction; Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, topological sheaves and locally topologically ringed spaces

proof.text: For any refinement, the original gluing with its refined open charts satisfies the refined overlap conditions. The canonical map from a gluing of the refined data to $\mathfrak T$ is obtained from the inclusions by Step 4. Conversely glue the refined charts lying in each original piece, and apply Step 4 first there and then on all original pieces to obtain the reverse map. Both composites are identities because they are identities on the refined open cover. These isomorphisms identify the maps and ideal subsheaves, since their restrictions agree and Step 4 and Step 5 give uniqueness. For successive restrictions or refinements, both comparison composites have these same local restrictions and hence coincide. This proves the claimed compatibility, including its coherence for successive refinements.
